symbols.name: n
symbols.def: The number of observed units.

symbols.name: \mathcal X
symbols.def: The measurable support of the covariate.

symbols.name: Y_0
symbols.def: The potential outcome under control.

symbols.name: Y_1
symbols.def: The potential outcome under treatment.

symbols.name: X
symbols.def: The observed pretreatment covariate.

symbols.name: D
symbols.def: The observed binary treatment indicator.

symbols.name: Y
symbols.def: The observed outcome.

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: The vector \(O=(Y,D,X)\).

symbols.name: O^{(n)}
symbols.def: The sample \(O^{(n)}=(O_1,\ldots,O_n)\).

symbols.name: P
symbols.def: A causal law inducing the observed law of \(O\).

symbols.name: P_X
symbols.def: The \(X\)-marginal of \(P\).

symbols.name: e
symbols.def: The function \(e(x)=P(D=1\mid X=x)\).

symbols.name: g_0
symbols.def: The function \(g_0(x)=E_P[Y\mid D=0,X=x]\).

symbols.name: g_1
symbols.def: The function \(g_1(x)=E_P[Y\mid D=1,X=x]\).

symbols.name: m_0
symbols.def: A deterministic function supplied with the experiment as a global approximation to \(g_0\).

symbols.name: m_1
symbols.def: A deterministic function supplied with the experiment as a global approximation to \(g_1\).

symbols.name: p
symbols.def: A deterministic function supplied with the experiment as a global approximation to \(e\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: The fixed uniform second-moment bound for the conditional treatment-effect signal \(g_1-g_0\).

symbols.name: \tau
symbols.def: The identified causal target \(\tau(P)=E_P[g_1(X)-g_0(X)]\), which is finite under \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\) and equals \(E_P[Y_1-Y_0]\) under consistency and conditional ignorability.

symbols.name: \kappa
symbols.def: The exponent governing left-boundary dyadic-shell mass.

symbols.name: \lambda_0
symbols.def: The fixed largest scale on which the shell law is imposed.

symbols.name: c_-
symbols.def: The class-wide lower multiplier for every dyadic shell.

symbols.name: c_+
symbols.def: The class-wide upper multiplier for every dyadic shell.

symbols.name: \eta_-
symbols.def: The fixed positive lower bound for the propensity in the bounded-overlap comparator experiment.

symbols.name: \eta_+
symbols.def: The fixed distance of the true propensity from one.

symbols.name: \sigma_0^2
symbols.def: The conditional residual-variance bound in the control arm.

symbols.name: \sigma_1^2
symbols.def: The conditional residual-variance bound in the treated arm.

symbols.name: M_Y
symbols.def: The uniform second-moment bound for the observed outcome.

symbols.name: r_{0n}
symbols.def: The supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) radius for \(m_0\).

symbols.name: r_{1n}
symbols.def: The supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) radius for \(m_1\).

symbols.name: r_{en}
symbols.def: The supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) radius for \(p\).

symbols.name: \bar r
symbols.def: A fixed class-wide upper bound for each supplied nuisance radius.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_n
symbols.def: The class of \((P,m_0,m_1,p)\) at sample size \(n\) defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}
symbols.def: The comparator class of \((P,m_0,m_1,p)\) with the same public-function information and bounded approximation radii, but with two-sided uniform overlap in place of dyadic left shells.

symbols.name: \lambda
symbols.def: A lower threshold for the treated inverse weight.

symbols.name: p^{\circ}
symbols.def: The projection \(p^{\circ}(x)=\min\{1-\eta_+/2,\max\{0,p(x)\}\}\).

symbols.name: q_{\lambda}
symbols.def: The denominator \(q_{\lambda}(x)=p^{\circ}(x)\vee\lambda\).

symbols.name: \psi_{\lambda}
symbols.def: The score defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_{\lambda}
symbols.def: The sample average of \(\psi_{\lambda}\).

symbols.name: b_{o,n}
symbols.def: The scale \(b_{o,n}=n^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\).

symbols.name: b_{e,n}
symbols.def: The scale \(b_{e,n}=r_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)}\).

symbols.name: b_{g,n}
symbols.def: The scale \(b_{g,n}=(n r_{1n}^2)^{-1}\), interpreted as \(+\infty\) when \(r_{1n}=0\).

symbols.name: \lambda_n^{\star}
symbols.def: The capped maximum of the active threshold components defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: Q_{\kappa}
symbols.def: The piecewise outcome-noise functional defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \rho_n
symbols.def: The four-channel frontier defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}
symbols.def: The median of five independent-block clipped estimators defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \mathcal T_n
symbols.def: The class of rules measurable in the observed sample and allowed to use the supplied public functions and certified radii.

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_n^{(1)}
symbols.def: The minimax absolute-error risk over \(\mathcal M_n\).

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_n^{(2)}
symbols.def: The minimax root-mean-squared risk over \(\mathcal M_n\).

symbols.name: \delta
symbols.def: A fixed probability level for minimax deviation risk.

symbols.name: \mathfrak R_{n,\delta}^{(\mathrm{prob})}
symbols.def: The smallest uniform \(\delta\)-error radius over all ATE estimators.

symbols.name: \mathcal I_n
symbols.def: The class of random-interval rules measurable in the observed sample and allowed to use the supplied public functions and certified radii.

symbols.name: \alpha
symbols.def: A fixed noncoverage probability.

symbols.name: \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
symbols.def: The oracle interval centered at \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}\) defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}
symbols.def: The shortest worst-case expected length among uniformly honest \((1-\alpha)\)-level intervals.

symbols.name: \beta_{\kappa}
symbols.def: The exponent of \(\rho_n\) when the three radii are polynomial in \(n\).

symbols.name: a_0
symbols.def: The exponent in \(r_{0n}=n^{-a_0}\).

symbols.name: a_1
symbols.def: The exponent in \(r_{1n}=n^{-a_1}\).

symbols.name: a_e
symbols.def: The exponent in \(r_{en}=n^{-a_e}\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: The benchmark \(B=\min\{1/2,a_1+a_e,a_0+a_e\}\).

symbols.name: \kappa_{\dagger}
symbols.def: The critical exponent defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lb}}
symbols.def: The four-channel shell localization algorithm defined by the corresponding definition.

symbols.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}
symbols.def: The dyadic comparison and validation strategy defined by the corresponding definition.

assumptions.condition: The coordinates of \(O^{(n)}\) are independent and identically distributed under the observed marginal induced by \(P\).
\(c_-u^{\kappa}\le P\{u/2<e(X)\le u\}\le c_+u^{\kappa}\) for every \(u\in(0,\lambda_0]\), with \(c_-\) and \(c_+\) fixed uniformly over the class and over \(n\).

novel.justification: The condition is satisfied by Beta-type propensity tails whose density is comparable to \(u^{\kappa-1}\), including rare-eligibility designs with a regularly varying participation margin.

The inequality holds for mixtures with two equal regularly varying tail reservoirs and a nonvanishing interior stratum, a concrete design class in which rare treatment arises in more than one covariate subgroup.
The inequality is satisfied by the same two-reservoir Beta-type mixtures after normalization and permits fixed interior mass without making the tail law degenerate.

definitions.name: \mathcal M_n
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n(\kappa,r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en};c_-,c_+,\lambda_0,\eta_+,\sigma_0^2,\sigma_1^2,M_Y,M,\bar r)=\{(P,m_0,m_1,p):(r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\text{ and, at sample size }n\text{, ass:iid, ass:consistency, ass:ignorability, ass:positivity, ass:uniform-shell, ass:right-overlap, ass:treated-residual-variance, ass:control-residual-variance, ass:outcome-second-moment, ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal, ass:public-g0-radius, ass:public-g1-radius, ass:public-e-radius, ass:lower-shell-richness, and ass:upper-shell-richness hold}\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}(r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en};\eta_-,\eta_+,\sigma_0^2,\sigma_1^2,M_Y,M,\bar r)=\{(P,m_0,m_1,p):(r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3,\ \eta_-+\eta_+<1,\text{ and, at sample size }n\text{, ass:iid, ass:consistency, ass:ignorability, ass:uniform-overlap-comparator, ass:treated-residual-variance, ass:control-residual-variance, ass:outcome-second-moment, ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal, ass:public-g0-radius, ass:public-g1-radius, and ass:public-e-radius hold}\}\).

definitions.name: \lambda_n^{\star}
definitions.construction: Let \(b_{o,n}=n^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\), \(b_{e,n}=r_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)}\), and \(b_{g,n}=(n r_{1n}^2)^{-1}\). Define \(\lambda_n^{\star}=\min\{\lambda_0,\max(b_{o,n},b_{e,n},b_{g,n})\}\) when \(0<\kappa\le1\), and \(\lambda_n^{\star}=\min\{\lambda_0,\max(b_{o,n},b_{e,n})\}\) when \(\kappa>1\).

definitions.name: \mathcal T_n
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal T_n=\{T:T(O^{(n)},m_0,m_1,p,r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in\mathbb R,\ O^{(n)}\mapsto T(O^{(n)},m_0,m_1,p,r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\text{ is measurable for every supplied }(m_0,m_1,p)\text{ and every }(r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\}\).

definitions.name: \widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}
definitions.construction: Partition \(O^{(n)}\) into five independent blocks whose sizes differ by at most one, compute \(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}^{(j)}\) from def:clipped-score on block \(j\) using the same public functions, and set \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}=\operatorname{median}_{1\le j\le5}\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}^{(j)}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal I_n
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal I_n=\{C:C(O^{(n)},m_0,m_1,p,r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\subseteq\mathbb R\text{ is an interval and }O^{(n)}\mapsto C(O^{(n)},m_0,m_1,p,r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\text{ is measurable for every supplied }(m_0,m_1,p)\text{ and every }(r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\}\).

definitions.name: \mathcal C_{n,\alpha}
definitions.construction: For \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\) and a constant \(K_{\alpha}\) depending only on \(\alpha\) and the supplied class constants, set \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}=[\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-K_{\alpha}\rho_n,\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}+K_{\alpha}\rho_n]\), and define \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}=\inf_{C_n\in\mathcal I_n:\inf_{\mathcal M_n}P\{\tau(P)\in C_n\}\ge1-\alpha}\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_n)]\).

definitions.name: \beta_{\kappa}
definitions.construction: Under \(r_{0n}=n^{-a_0}\), \(r_{1n}=n^{-a_1}\), and \(r_{en}=n^{-a_e}\), define \(\beta_{\kappa}=\min\{1/2,\,\kappa/2+(1-\kappa)a_1\;\mathbf 1\{0<\kappa<1\}\text{ with this entry omitted for }\kappa\ge1,\,a_1+\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)],\,a_1+\kappa a_e/(\kappa+2),\,a_0+a_e\}\).

definitions.name: \kappa_{\dagger}
definitions.construction: Let \(B=\min\{1/2,a_1+a_e,a_0+a_e\}\). If \(B\le a_1\), set \(\kappa_{\dagger}=0\). If \(x=B-a_1>0\), set \(\kappa_{\dagger}=\max\{x/(1/2-a_1),2x/(1-2x),2x/(a_e-x)\}\), interpreting a nonpositive denominator as \(+\infty\).

definitions.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lb}}
definitions.construction: Build four subexperiments inside \(\mathcal M_n\): shell-localized treated-mean shifts for \(Q_{\kappa}\), an untreated-observation coupling at scale \(n^{-1/(\kappa+1)}\), a signed-cell fuzzy mixture at scale \(r_{en}^{2/(\kappa+2)}\) whose propensity tilt cancels its sign tilt in each observed row, and the analogous regular-cell control mixture. In every family calibrate the sole nonzero regression perturbation so that its \(L^2(P_X)\) norm is bounded by the applicable nuisance radius or by a fixed constant no larger than \(M^{1/2}\); combine the probability separations by a maximum-to-sum comparison.

definitions.name: \mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}
definitions.construction: Use a dyadic family of \(\widehat\tau_{\lambda}\), sample-split empirical shell counts, and held-out prediction-risk certificates in a Lepski or aggregation comparison to derive a data-driven threshold and the smallest uniform oracle-inequality penalty relative to \(\rho_n\).

statements.statement: There are constants depending only on \((c_-,c_+,\kappa,\lambda_0)\) such that, uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n\) and \(0<\lambda\le\lambda_0\), \(P\{e(X)\le\lambda\}\asymp\lambda^{\kappa}\) and \(E_P[(e(X)\vee\lambda)^{-1}]\asymp v_{\kappa}(\lambda)^2\), where \(v_{\kappa}(\lambda)=\lambda^{-(1-\kappa)/2}\) for \(0<\kappa<1\), \(v_1(\lambda)=\sqrt{1+\log(\lambda_0/\lambda)}\), and \(v_{\kappa}(\lambda)=1\) for \(\kappa>1\).
statements.justification: This converts the primitive dyadic law into the two uniform tail functionals used on both sides of the frontier.
statements.gap: KhanTamer2010Irregular gives tail-rate intuition but not this class-uniform dyadic-shell equivalence.
statements.consumer: The clipped-score upper bound and every shell-localized lower family use these uniform comparisons.

statements.statement: For every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), the rule \(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}\) from def:clipped-score and def:oracle-threshold belongs to \(\mathcal T_n\). There is a constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on the fixed class constants, including \(M\) and \(M_Y\), such that \(\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}E_P|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}-\tau(P)|\le C\rho_n\). The same estimator satisfies \(\sup_{\mathcal M_n}P\{|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}-\tau(P)|>C\rho_n/\delta\}\le\delta\) for every fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\).
statements.justification: It supplies one feasible procedure attaining all four components without strengthening global \(L^2(P_X)\) information.
statements.gap: Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves a sufficient studentized limit, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, gives asymptotic inference for a bias-corrected trimmed ATE estimator that preserves the original target; neither establishes the finite-risk public-function upper frontier obtained from the \(r_{1n}/\sqrt{n\lambda}\) stochastic term.
statements.consumer: Analysts with certified black-box prediction errors obtain a clipping rule for the original population ATE rather than a trimmed-population estimand.

statements.statement: The median rule \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal T_n\). If each of its five independent-block copies of \(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}\) has mean absolute error at most \(K\rho_n\), then \(P\{|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)|>u\}\le\min\{1,10(K\rho_n/u)^3\}\) and \(\{E_P(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P))^2\}^{1/2}\le\sqrt{21}\,K\rho_n\).
statements.justification: The amplification converts a first-moment upper bound into the root-MSE half of the sharp theorem without an unassumed fourth moment.
statements.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR does not isolate this finite-block root-MSE upgrade for a weak-overlap public-function rate.
statements.consumer: The minimax root-MSE theorem can use the same clipped construction under only the stated second-moment envelope.

statements.statement: For every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), the handle \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lb}}\) yields constants \(c>0\) and \(\delta_0\in(0,1/4)\), uniform in \(n\), such that every rule \(T\in\mathcal T_n\), including every rule using \(O^{(n)}\), \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), and the certified radii, obeys \(\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}P\{|T(O^{(n)},m_0,m_1,p,r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})-\tau(P)|\ge c\rho_n\}\ge\delta_0\). Consequently \(\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}\ge c\delta_0\rho_n\) and \(\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\ge c\sqrt{\delta_0}\rho_n\). Every fixed-sign law used by the fuzzy mixtures, rather than merely the mixtures themselves, belongs to \(\mathcal M_n\). Each of the four subexperiment families satisfies \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\) by regression-amplitude calibration within the applicable nuisance radius or a sufficiently small fixed constant.
statements.justification: This shell-matching converse certifies all four obstructions against the full public-information decision class.
statements.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE provide fuzzy-hypothesis templates, but not the shell-preserving collision and empty-treatment channels for this ATE experiment.
statements.consumer: The lower bound certifies that no estimator using the sample and the same public predictions can remove any one of the four rate components.

statements.statement: Uniformly over the bounded radius regime \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\) and the fixed reservoir-rich shell constants, with every minimax infimum taken over \(T\in\mathcal T_n\) measurable in the observed sample and allowed to use \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), and the certified radii, \(\mathfrak R_n^{(1)}\asymp\rho_n\), \(\mathfrak R_n^{(2)}\asymp\rho_n\), and \(\mathfrak R_{n,\delta}^{(\mathrm{prob})}\asymp\rho_n\) for every fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\). Thus the same \(\rho_n\) is the sharp frontier for absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, and fixed-probability error.
statements.justification: It closes the exact global-prediction price of one-sided weak overlap across three operational loss criteria.
statements.gap: The closest regular-overlap benchmarks are JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE; no located weak-overlap paper has this matched public-function frontier.
statements.consumer: Method developers can use the theorem as the oracle benchmark for clipping, robustification, and any proposed higher-order correction.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) and every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), a choice of \(K_{\alpha}\) depending only on the supplied radii and fixed class constants makes \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\) uniformly honest: \(\inf_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}\ge1-\alpha\), with \(\sup_{\mathcal M_n}E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})]\le C_{\alpha}\rho_n\). Conversely every uniformly honest rule \(C_n\in\mathcal I_n\), including every rule using the public functions and certified radii, has worst-case expected length at least \(c_{\alpha}\rho_n\), so \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\).
statements.justification: Risk optimality alone does not answer the inferential price; this theorem makes honest expected length obey the same frontier.
statements.gap: Rothe2017RobustCI uses finite-cell small-sample structure, Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves asymptotic Wald validity, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1, proves asymptotic normality after bias-corrected trimming; none calibrates the four-channel minimax bias radius or proves a matching honest-length converse.
statements.consumer: Applied work that must retain the full population can report an honest bias-aware interval rather than trim the target or invoke a Gaussian approximation in a bias-dominated regime.

statements.statement: If \(r_{0n}=n^{-a_0}\), \(r_{1n}=n^{-a_1}\), and \(r_{en}=n^{-a_e}\) with \(a_0,a_1,a_e\ge0\), then the bounded-radius regime holds for \(\bar r\ge1\), and \(\rho_n=n^{-\beta_{\kappa}}\) up to the boundary logarithm specified below. If \(B\le a_1\), weak overlap causes no polynomial deterioration. If \(B>a_1\), then \(\beta_{\kappa}<B\) holds exactly when \(0<\kappa<\kappa_{\dagger}\). At \(\kappa=1\), the additional factor is \(\sqrt{1+\log_+(n r_{1n}^2)}\), and it changes the leading root-\(n\) rate only when \(a_1<1/2\). The empty-shell exponent \(a_1+\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]\) tends to \(a_1+1/2\), so its surviving fast-tail term never worsens the benchmark \(B\).
statements.justification: The critical exponent turns the rate formula into a falsifiable regime map for when weak overlap truly changes attainable accuracy.
statements.gap: KhanTamer2010Irregular has tail-dependent rates but not this joint nuisance phase boundary with the empty-treated-shell exponent \(a_1+\kappa/[2(\kappa+1)]\).
statements.consumer: A researcher can diagnose from estimated learning-rate exponents whether overlap or ordinary nuisance interaction is the binding statistical bottleneck.

statements.statement: For every fixed \(\kappa>0\), \(\mathcal M_n\cap\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}=\varnothing\): ass:uniform-shell places positive mass below every positive propensity threshold, whereas ass:uniform-overlap-comparator imposes \(e(X)\ge\eta_-\) almost surely. For fixed \(n\) and \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), \(\lim_{\kappa\to\infty}\rho_n=(1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\asymp n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\), uniformly under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\). The last display is the known bounded-overlap public-function benchmark of JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE. Thus the relation is a fast-tail rate reduction between distinct experiments, not a class inclusion.
statements.justification: This known-comparator proposition records both the strict class separation and the exact surviving treated empty-shell term needed for a valid standard-case check.
statements.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, establish the bounded-overlap product-rate benchmark; JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds, Section 6.1 and the conclusion, identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open direction. The new theorem concerns the separate dyadic-shell experiment rather than reproving that benchmark.
statements.consumer: Readers can distinguish the genuinely weak-overlap class from the bounded-overlap comparator while checking that the four-channel formula has the correct fast-tail benchmark.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{adapt}}\), determine the smallest deterministic penalty sequence \(\ell_n\ge1\) for which a fully data-driven estimator and confidence interval, not given \(\kappa\), \(c_-\), \(c_+\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), or \(r_{en}\), attain uniform risk and honest expected length at most \(C\ell_n\rho_n\) over compact ranges of these indices; prove a matching adaptation lower bound for \(\ell_n\).
statements.justification: The oracle theorem exposes but does not resolve the practical cost of learning which of the four obstructions is active.
statements.gap: MaWang2020RobustIPW has data-driven trimming for an IPW asymptotic criterion, while the supplied theorem assumes known shell and nuisance certificates; no exact adaptation penalty is available.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether the oracle clipping and interval benchmarks can be implemented from validation data without an avoidable logarithmic loss.

sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational sample augmented by deterministic public nuisance functions \((m_0,m_1,p)\), supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) error radii bounded by the fixed cap \(\bar r\), a fixed signal envelope \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\), and decision rules that may use all public inputs.
sampling_model.units: Independent units \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), from a causal law satisfying consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with propensity \(e(X)\), positive almost surely and allowed to approach zero.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform one-sided dyadic shells satisfy \(c_-u^{\kappa}\le P\{u/2<e(X)\le u\}\le c_+u^{\kappa}\) for \(0<u\le\lambda_0\), while \(e(X)\le1-\eta_+\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The minimax infima range over rules measurable in \(O^{(n)}\) that also receive the supplied \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), and \(r_{en}\). The same public inputs are held fixed throughout each lower family, and the certified radii lie in \([0,\bar r]\).

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the parametric-plus-nuisance-product structure-agnostic treatment-effect rate under a propensity bounded away from zero.
Section 2 gives the pure structure-agnostic ATE benchmark consisting of the parametric floor plus the nuisance-product rate under regular overlap.
Thresholded AIPW is uniformly asymptotically normal under sufficient weak-overlap nuisance conditions.
IPW has Gaussian or stable limits according to tail and trimming regimes.
Localized fuzzy hypotheses yield a minimax lower bound for pointwise CATE.
Inverse-weight estimation can have tail-dependent irregular rates.
Limited-overlap confidence accuracy is driven by local comparison-cell sizes.
Section 6.1 treats bounded-overlap ATE examples, while the conclusion identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and a studentized Gaussian limit for bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimators targeting the original treatment-effect estimand, with Proposition B.1 verifying the ATE specialization.

tldr: Global prediction accuracy does not determine the attainable accuracy of the population ATE once treated observations become polynomially rare. In a public-function experiment with fixed, bounded global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates, a fixed \(L^2(P_X)\) envelope for the conditional treatment-effect signal, and uniform one-sided propensity shells, the proposed theorem identifies a four-channel frontier \(\rho_n\): tail-amplified outcome noise, regression error hidden in shells with no treated observations, localized propensity--treated-regression uncertainty, and the regular control-side nuisance interaction. The minimax decision class consists of measurable rules using the sample, public functions, and certified radii. A clipped doubly robust average attains absolute and fixed-probability risk, a five-block median attains root mean-squared risk, and a bias-aware interval has matching honest expected length. The open sequel asks for the exact cost of adapting to unknown shell and nuisance certificates.

project_justification.gap: Regular-overlap structure-agnostic theory gives a nuisance-product benchmark, while weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, is especially close on target preservation: its bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust method retains the original ATE and yields asymptotic inference, but it does not characterize global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax risk or an honest-length converse frontier. None of the opened papers characterizes minimax absolute risk, root mean-squared risk, fixed-probability error, and honest interval length for the same full-population ATE under bounded global prediction-error certificates, a fixed conditional-effect signal envelope, an explicit public-information decision class, and uniform one-sided shells.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model separates what a learner knows globally from where treated observations actually occur. A fixed bound \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\) makes the ATE functional finite without imposing a pointwise or armwise outcome envelope. The left tail generates three treated-side obstructions with different scales, while the control-side product channel remains regular.
project_justification.fill: The core supplies an explicit public-information decision class, bounded nuisance radii, a fixed treatment-effect signal moment envelope, a single clipped estimator, a median amplification, four in-class converse channels whose regression amplitudes satisfy that envelope, the polynomial deterioration threshold, and an oracle bias-aware interval, all indexed by \(\rho_n\).

related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, is the closest public-function experiment: it gives the doubly robust structure-agnostic rate when the propensity is bounded away from zero, and its asymmetric fuzzy hypotheses inform the dyadic-reservoir converse. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, studies pure and smoothness-augmented black-box classes under regular overlap. The shell class is disjoint from the bounded-overlap public-function class, but Proposition 8 shows that its fast-tail rate limit retains \(r_{1n}/\sqrt n\) and is uniformly equivalent, under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\), to their parametric-plus-product benchmark. JinSyrgkanis2025GeneralLinearFunctionalLowerBounds, Section 6.1 and the conclusion, broadens structure-agnostic lower bounds while retaining bounded-overlap ATE examples and expressly identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as open; it supplies the regime-opening anchor rather than a theorem matched here. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics gives a clipped cross-fitted AIPW Gaussian limit under sufficient tail and nuisance conditions; it informs the upper score but is not a risk comparator. MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1, constructs a bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimator that preserves the original ATE and establishes asymptotic linearity and normal inference; it does not give the global-\(L^2\) public-function minimax-risk frontier or the matching honest-length converse. MaWang2020RobustIPW derives Gaussian and stable IPW limits and a data-driven trimming rule, while the oracle theorem has two public nuisance errors and a full-population minimax target. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE provides the localized fuzzy-hypothesis method for a different estimand and smoothness class. KhanTamer2010Irregular explains why support tails govern inverse-weight rates. Rothe2017RobustCI motivates local effective sample size and limited-overlap coverage, but its robust intervals rely on finite-cell or auxiliary distributional structure rather than the four-channel global-\(L^2\) radius.
technical_internal_limitation: The lower frontier is restricted to reservoir-rich fixed shell constants satisfying ass:lower-shell-richness and ass:upper-shell-richness. Each lower family must also calibrate its regression perturbation to satisfy ass:bounded-treatment-effect-signal. The supplied constructions do so because the sole nonzero regression has \(L^2(P_X)\) norm within the relevant nuisance radius or a sufficiently small fixed constant. The upper bound needs only uniform shells and the fixed signal moment, so arbitrarily tight admissible shell constants may have a different converse geometry.
honest_scope: The main theorem treats supplied public functions, bounded certified radii, fixed shell constants, and the primitive signal condition \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\le M\); it imposes no stronger pointwise or armwise potential-outcome envelope and makes no Wald or asymptotic-normality claim. The minimax rules may use every supplied public input. Adaptation to unknown calibration, bounded-outcome variants, arbitrary shell constants, and the exact studentized-validity region remain open. The dyadic-shell and bounded-overlap classes share the signal condition but are distinct; the fast-tail analytic limit is \((1+r_{1n})n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\), which is uniformly equivalent to the known regular-overlap structure-agnostic rate under \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\).

seed_details.seed: Four-channel sharp public-function ATE frontier under one-sided weak overlap
seed_details.anchor_locator: The sharp-theorem note sections on the theorem and upper bound, Least-favourable families, and Honest inference sections; Jin and Syrgkanis, Introduction, equations (1)--(9), Theorem 1, proof outline in Section 4, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The operator note corrects the treated-regression stochastic term to \(r_1/\sqrt{n\lambda}\), fixes uniform dyadic-shell constants, and gives four shell-localized converse channels. Jin and Syrgkanis establish the regular-overlap public-nuisance benchmark by asymmetric fuzzy hypotheses, but their overlap condition keeps the propensity uniformly away from zero.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the regular-overlap fuzzy alternatives by shell-preserving two-point and collision-controlled mixtures, and use the exact upper stochastic term by the exact conditional second-moment bound.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for structure-agnostic ATE minimax weak overlap, one-sided propensity shells, and public nuisance functions located regular-overlap minimax papers and weak-overlap limit theorems, but no matched four-channel risk theorem.
seed_details.referee_objection: This is immediate from Jin and Syrgkanis because weak overlap only changes constants in their doubly robust remainder.
seed_details.rebuttal: The objection fails because the inverse score has a tail-indexed variance channel, an empty-treated-shell channel, and a localized nuisance-product channel with distinct exponents; none is bounded uniformly by the regular-overlap product remainder.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The claim is uniform over a fixed shell class, not a single witness; the estimator, rate, four converse channels, fixed-probability risk, and honest interval length are named focal objects.

seed_details.seed: Adaptive weak-overlap ATE frontier with unknown tail and nuisance radii
seed_details.anchor_locator: Honest inference and framing, where adaptation to unknown tail and radii is explicitly excluded; threshold scales \(b_o\), \(b_e\), and \(b_g\).
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The oracle clip is the maximum of three qualitatively different scales, so replacing it by a data-driven selector changes the first upper-bound step and may incur a testing penalty across shell exponents.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace the deterministic oracle threshold by simultaneous dyadic estimator comparisons with empirical tail counts and held-out prediction-risk certificates.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for adaptive clipped AIPW with unknown overlap exponent and Lepski selection found threshold-indexed IPW inference in Ma and Wang and sufficient clipping rules in Dorn, but no oracle inequality against the corrected \(\rho_n\).
seed_details.referee_objection: Ma and Wang already choose trimming by empirical mean squared error.
seed_details.rebuttal: Their selector concerns an IPW asymptotic bias--variance criterion, whereas the desired oracle simultaneously adapts to two black-box nuisance radii and the empty-treated-shell obstruction for the untrimmed population ATE.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The adaptive penalty is left as an open object with a concrete Lepski handle rather than asserted to be logarithmic.

seed_details.anchor_locator: Introduction, Assumptions 3--4, Theorem 1 and Corollary 1, proof discussion near the clipped remainder bound, the explicit lax-bound remark in the appendix, and Conclusion.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: Dorn proves oracle equivalence and uniform Gaussian approximation under sufficient clipping and nuisance-rate conditions, and explicitly states that one propensity-rate bound may be lax.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Turn the sufficient clipped-score remainder inequalities into a sharp boundary by constructing studentization-aligned nuisance alternatives outside the candidate region.
seed_details.destination_search: Searches for necessary weak-overlap AIPW nuisance rates found Ma and Wang's IPW regimes and standard DML product-rate theory, but no necessity theorem for two estimated AIPW nuisances.
seed_details.referee_objection: This only sharpens a technical rate condition in Dorn.
seed_details.rebuttal: A necessity construction would distinguish a proof artifact from a statistical obstruction and would produce an iff phase diagram for uniform studentized normality, which the published theorem expressly does not give.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: The limit law and iff validity region are the kernel; it is not repackaged as another minimax-risk claim.

seed_details.seed: Bounded-outcome replacement of the Gaussian least-favourable channels
seed_details.anchor_locator: Least-favourable families and the final paragraph excluding bounded-treatment-effect variants.
seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The supplied converse uses Gaussian treated noise and signed mean perturbations; bounded Bernoulli or Rademacher channels change the first divergence calculation while leaving the shell allocations meaningful.
seed_details.changed_proof_step: Replace Gaussian mean-shift Kullback--Leibler calculations by bounded likelihood-ratio calculations while preserving the public-function cancellation identity.
seed_details.destination_search: The bounded-response constructions in Kennedy et al. and the bounded-overlap results in Jin and Syrgkanis do not establish the one-sided shell rate.
seed_details.referee_objection: Binary outcomes already appear in structure-agnostic lower bounds, so this is a routine recoding.
seed_details.rebuttal: The recoding must preserve four simultaneous shell constraints and the one-row mixture cancellation; it is credible but narrower than resolving the unrestricted frontier first.
seed_details.anti_pattern_check: Dropped from the first paper because it is a restriction-robustness sequel, not because the mathematical question is vacuous.

seed_details.opened_anchor_evidence: The upper theorem needs only uniform shell constants, while the current converse requires extra numerical room for an untouched reservoir; tighter nonempty shell classes may suppress individual obstructions.

literature_map: The selected kernel was checked against four adjacent threads. Jin and Syrgkanis (2025, Theorem 1, Remark 2, and Section 4) prove structure-agnostic optimality for weighted treatment effects under a propensity bounded away from zero; their asymmetric fuzzy hypotheses inform the public-function converse, but not its shell localization. The bounded-overlap comparator \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{reg}}\) carries the same sample, public functions, certified radii, signal moment bound, and other moment conditions as the shell experiment, but the two classes are disjoint because the shell condition puts positive mass below every positive threshold. Bonvini, Kennedy, Dukes, and Balakrishnan (2024, Section 2 and the hybrid-class results) give the regular-overlap black-box benchmark and a smoothness-assisted correction, not a one-sided tail experiment. The exact fast-tail limit of \(\rho_n\) retains \(r_{1n}/\sqrt n\); the fixed cap \(r_{1n}\le\bar r\) makes it uniformly equivalent to the published parametric-plus-product benchmark without altering the polynomial phase diagram. Dorn (2025, Theorem 1, Corollary 1, and the open remark in the proof) proves sufficient Gaussian inference for clipped AIPW and leaves a propensity-rate restriction potentially lax; it neither states global minimax risk nor a matching converse. Ma, Sant’Anna, Sasaki, and Ura (2026, Theorem 3.1 and Proposition B.1) use trimming plus a sieve bias correction to retain the original ATE and obtain asymptotic linearity and normal inference under weak overlap; they do not formulate the law--public-function experiment, its global-\(L^2\) minimax risks, or an honest expected-length converse. Ma and Wang (2020, Theorem 1 and Proposition 1) derive Gaussian and stable IPW regimes and data-driven trimming, but do not analyze two black-box nuisance errors. Kennedy, Balakrishnan, Robins, and Wasserman (2024, Theorem 1, Proposition 2, and the lower-bound roadmap) supply the localized fuzzy-hypothesis template; their target is pointwise CATE in a Holder class. Khan and Tamer (2010) establish the tail-dependent irregularity background, while Rothe (2017) studies locally small effective samples and robust intervals under finite-cell and auxiliary distributional structure. Jin and Syrgkanis (2025, Section 6.1 and the conclusion) retain bounded-overlap ATE examples in their general-functional theory and name weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension. No closer paper found through September 2026 subsumes the four-channel public-function frontier.
novelty_justification: The exact unoccupied object is the minimax risk of the full-population ATE over law--public-function pairs with bounded global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates, a fixed \(L^2(P_X)\) conditional-effect signal envelope, an explicit public-information decision class, and a fixed uniform one-sided dyadic-shell law. Relative to JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR and BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, the shell experiment is disjoint from their bounded-overlap classes and adds three treated-side obstructions beyond the regular product remainder: tail-amplified outcome noise, regression error hidden where no treated observation arrives, and a shell-localized propensity--regression mixture. Relative to Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics, MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, and MaWang2020RobustIPW, the target is a matched global-risk and honest-length frontier rather than a sufficient limit-law region or a bias-corrected trimming construction. The theorem uses the \(r_{1n}/\sqrt{n\lambda}\) stochastic term, fixed class-wide shell constants, collision-controlled fuzzy mixtures calibrated to the signal envelope, explicit cap cases, and median amplification. Proposition 8 is labeled as a known-comparator reduction: its exact fast-tail limit retains \(r_{1n}/\sqrt n\), and bounded radii absorb that term into the parametric order. The comparator table otherwise marks adjacent papers as technique ancestors.
